close_reason: Mechanism verified end to end; two inferences refuted (missing metadata isn't fatal; failed connect doesn't stick); server-down = ~45s then Fail, so reachability must be checked before a run.

comments.text:
Done 2026-09-25 (aarch64-darwin, pinned buck2 7600cb80, bazel-remote 2.6.2). Full table: https://github.com/firefly-engineering/turnkey/blob/56e05c0a5905/docs/research/test-cache-mechanism-feasibility.md#verification-run-turnkey-w5510-2026-09-25 . The ADR 0001 consequences were corrected in the same commit.

Setup: a throwaway buck2 project; a rule emitting ExternalRunnerTestInfo with supports_test_execution_caching and the cache-reading default_executor; the OSS runner; an ActionResult written by hand under the digest buck2 reported. All removed afterwards.

Facts later tickets depend on:
- CONFIRMED: engine_address pointed at bazel-remote works (Capabilities + AC lookup; no Execution service needed). A hand-written pass is served as a hit: not executed, recorded stdout printed, original duration shown, what-ran says 'cache'. The hit survives the same daemon, a daemon restart, buck2 clean, and another checkout path. bazel-remote accepts inline-stdout entries with AC validation on.
- A recorded failure is replayed as a failure without running (only passes may be written).
- REFUTED: a missing execution_metadata does not fail the test (served as Pass 0.0s); it only loses the duration.
- REFUTED: a failed connect does not stick. The same daemon recovers once the server is back.
- Server down (fresh daemon, or killed under a connected one): about 45 s of connection retries, then every opted-in test reports Fail (exit 32) without executing.
- Reads skipped (--no-remote-cache) with the server down: the test runs locally and passes, no connection attempt, identical digest reported. The uncached fallback and 'force re-run, still record' both work.
- NOT TESTED: a missing output (the OSS runner requests none); entries referencing CAS blobs.

title: Does the recording mechanism work end to end on one test target?
